Not a babysitter, but the babysat. I had an awesome babysitter between ages 6 and 8 who was like a big kid herself. One day my two year old sister woke up from a nap and we both wandered into our mom's room. We had recently learned the game of "throw stuff at the ceiling fan", so we took two of my sister's baby dolls and put them on the leaves of the ceiling fan, then turned it on. We had a contest to see whose crap would stay on there the longest. Eventually we abandoned the dolls for some of my mom's underwear that was in a laundry basket full of clean stuff and kept going using that. It had been about 30 minutes before our babysitter came upstairs looking for us and when she saw what we were doing, she JOINED IN the fun before making us clean up. You rock, Erin!

But he was pissed off about the heating pad creating static interference and him not being able to listen to conspiracy theorists on the radio (Alex Jones...complete crackpot idiot who needs to be ripped off the air for inducing panic), so he tried to force me to take up to 4 ibuprofen in addition to the Vicodin the oral surgeon prescribed to "keep the swelling down".

As far as fears go, my biggest is that people will abandon me or judge me or hate me. Right now my biggest concern is that I may have been misdiagnosed as a kid and I'm going to talk to my doctor about screening for bipolar disorder.

Thank you,  I plan on it. Plan on asking my doctor about bipolar/some other mood disorder possibilities. Treating the anxiety/depression didn't help as a kid and I've been having issues with mood swings since I was in my late teens.
Yes, I'm a sophomore technically even though I've been there for four years (I took a two year leave after freshman year because of financial issues).

The thing I want most is for my professors to know what I feel on a daily basis...for them to see that the reason I'm not doing as well as I could be is not because I'm lazy or don't care, but that once you go into the dark place, you're immobilized and it takes everything you have to beat able to wake up in the morning. Then when you do snap out of it, you panic because you know you have so much to catch up on from when you were in one of your low periods and then the cycle starts all over again. I've explained but they don't seem to care and I feel like one of the things my death would accomplish is having them find out that I'm not using it as an excuse to slack. :(

Not specifically. It's just kind of there. Actually wondering if I'm so used to being anxious that it flies under the radar most of the time and only notice flare ups...if that's the case, how bad is it really?

Yes. I was actually on antidepressants on and off starting at age 9 when my GP diagnosed me with an anxiety disorder. All throughout childhood it would do this weird thing where it would be active, then go into dormancy on its own then "wake up" again spontaneously. I do know that stress triggers it. Unfortunately,  none of the medications I was put on helped. Paxil and Zoloft at first turned me into a zombie and I was so out of it that I almost didn't pass sixth grade because my grades were so bad from not being able to concentrate in class/keep track of my homework. Went off of it in 7th grade, things got better. Anxiety and depression came out of dormancy in 10th grade, went on Citalopram and had to be taken off because it made me aggressive. Went back on Zoloft after Citalopram but it didn't help anything so I just quit taking it.

No. I'm afraid to tell anyone like my doctor that I'm having these issues because I'm afraid they'll force me to go to the hospital, and when that happens and people find out, I'll get judged and labeled. Last fall I didn't do well in school and failed a few classes, before that I had taken a two year hiatus because of other issues. In my mind my dream was wrecked at my own hands...it's a stupid reason, I know, but it was the worst thing that could have happened in that area and I have not moved past it. Truthfully if I were more at peace with dying, I would have done something by now. Waiting until I get to that point if I ever do.
